facts.statement: Zalmoxes lived during the Late Cretaceous (Maastrichtian age) in what is now Romania.
facts.quote: Zalmoxes is a genus of probable rhabdodontid ornithopod dinosaur from the Maastrichtian age of the Late Cretaceous in what is now Romania.

facts.statement: The genus was first named in 1899 by Franz Nopcsa as the species Mochlodon robustum.
facts.quote: The genus is known from specimens first named as the species Mochlodon robustum in 1899 by Franz Nopcsa before being reclassified as Rhabdodon robustum by him in 1915.

facts.statement: The species was reclassified as Zalmoxes robustus in 2003.
facts.quote: In 2003, the species was once more reclassified as the type species Zalmoxes robustus.

facts.statement: The genus name honors the Dacian deity Zalmoxis, while the species name refers to the robustness of the fossil remains.
facts.quote: The generic name refers to the Dacian deity Zalmoxis and the specific name robustus refers to the robustness of the remains.

facts.statement: Numerous fossils found in Transylvania were first named in 1899 by Baron Franz Nopcsa.
facts.quote: Zalmoxes was first known from numerous fossils found in Transylvania, which were named as the species Mochlodon robustus by Baron Franz Nopcsa in 1899.

facts.statement: A new species was identified in 2003 based on new remains found in Romania by Weishampel et al.
facts.quote: Weishampel et al. (2003) published a paper on new remains from Romania, which they found to represent a new species.

facts.statement: In 2026, the species Zalmoxes shqiperorum was reclassified as a ceratopsian dinosaur and renamed Ferenceratops.
facts.quote: In 2026, this species was determined to be a ceratopsian dinosaur as opposed to an ornithopod, and given the new generic name Ferenceratops.

facts.statement: Zalmoxes was a small, bipedal herbivore characterized by a large triangular head and a beak.
facts.quote: Zalmoxes is a rather small genus of bipedal herbivore with a large triangular head and a beak.

facts.statement: Subadult Zalmoxes robustus measured between 2 and 2.4 meters in total body length.
facts.quote: The subadult Z. robustus range from 2 - 2.4 m in total body length.

facts.statement: Adult Zalmoxes robustus reached up to 2.5 meters in length and 45 kilograms in body mass.
facts.quote: An adult Z. robustus would have measured up to 2.5 m in length and 45 kg in body mass.

facts.statement: An unnamed species of Zalmoxes is known from adults reaching 2.9 meters in length.
facts.quote: An unnamed species of Zalmoxes, is known from larger sizes, with an adult 2.9 m in length.

facts.statement: Approximately 80% of the skull of Z. robustus is known from fossils.
facts.quote: Z. robustus is known from about 80% of the skull.

facts.statement: No complete articulated skull of Z. robustus is known, as most bones are found isolated.
facts.quote: However, no complete articulated skull is known, and most of the bones do not overlap and are found in isolation.

facts.statement: Only two mostly complete skeletons of Z. shqiperorum are known: a holotype adult and a referred juvenile.
facts.quote: Only two mostly complete skeletons are known, the holotype adult, and a referred juvenile.

facts.statement: Ossified tendons found in a juvenile Z. shqiperorum were circular or elliptical in cross-section and had fine striations.
facts.quote: Ossified tendons are known from the juvenile specimen, showing that they were circular or elliptical in cross section and have fine striations in Z. shqiperorum.

facts.statement: In 2003, Weishampel et al. established the family Rhabdodontidae for Mochlodon, Rhabdodon, and Zalmoxes.
facts.quote: In 2003, Weishampel et al. named a new family for Mochlodon, Rhabdodon and the new genus Zalmoxes.

facts.statement: The family Rhabdodontidae is classified as a derived group within Iguanodontia.
facts.quote: This family, Rhabdodontidae, was placed as a derived within Iguanodontia.

facts.statement: Nopcsa proposed that Zalmoxes adapted through insular dwarfism because it was smaller than its relatives in the Hateg Basin.
facts.quote: Nopcsa proposed that the animals of the Hateg Basin, which were smaller than their relatives elsewhere, adapted through insular dwarfism.

facts.statement: Zalmoxes fossils are found in the Sânpetru, Sebes, and Densuş-Ciula Formations in the Hateg Island region of Romania.
facts.quote: Fossils of Zalmoxes have been unearthed in the Sânpetru Formation, the Sebes Formation and Densuş-Ciula Formation in Romania, all of which are in the Hateg Island region.

facts.statement: A 2003 study suggested Zalmoxes ate tough fibrous plants including soft shoots, horsetails, angiosperms, pteridophytes, and ferns.

facts.statement: Further studies indicated Zalmoxes could process and digest C3 plants.
facts.quote: Further studies showed that it could process and digest C3 plants.

facts.statement: It is debated whether Zalmoxes shqiperorum is an ornithopod or a ceratopsian, with recent studies in 2026 placing it in Ceratopsia.
facts.quote: In 2026, this species was determined to be a ceratopsian dinosaur as opposed to an ornithopod, and given the new generic name Ferenceratops.
